 Abando has always been in Cone’s radar
 By Richard Dy
 November 13, 2026
 40
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 PHILIPPINE coach Tim Cone made it clear that high-leaping wingman Rhenz Abando has always been “in the radar” for inclusion to the national team even though the former NCAA Most Valuable Player was out of the Gilas Pilipinas loop for the last three years.
 The American mentor said that Abando was part of the original Gilas 12 he considered when he took over the coaching reins of the Philippine team after Chot Reyes stepped down after the 2023 FIBA World Cup, which the Philippines co-hosted with Japan and Indonesia.
 “He was part of the original 12 when we first put the team together almost three years ago, how time flies,” Cone told The Manila Times, in referring to Abando, who on Wednesday, was named to the Gilas Pilipinas final 12 that will be competing against Syria on Nov. 27 in the fifth window of the FIBA World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers.
 “But he injured his back at that time and ultimately wasn’t included. So he’s always been on our radar,” he said.
 Cone added that with TNT gunner Calvin Oftana not playing for Gilas Pilipinas in the coming November window because his wife is set to give birth, Abando was among the players who were considered, along with Robert Bolick, Jordan Heading and Zavier Lucero.

 “When we lost Calvin, we felt he (Abando) was the closest to playing like Calvin, position-wise. We considered others, of course, like Bolick, Heading, Lucero and outside the pool and some of those in the pool that didn’t make the 12, like RJ (Abarrientos), Balty (Justine Baltazar), (Justin) Araña, and Troy (Rosario),” Cone said.
 “Again, position-wise, we were looking to replace Calvin. If we had to replace a point guard or a big, we probably would have considered someone else.”
 Advertisement 
 Abando currently plays for the Anyang Jung Kwan Jang Red Boosters where he averages 10.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.9 steals, and 1.4 blocks per game in the Korean Basketball League.
 The 6-foot-2 Abando averaged 5.2 points and 2.2 rebounds in his last Gilas Pilipinas stint during the 2023 FIBA World Cup in Manila.
 The Philippines went on to finish 24th out of 32 nations in that tournament.
